An illustrated step-by-step manual with screenshots — saved into your Downloads and opened, so it stays on the phone
A quick tour of every screen. Everything works offline; data leaves the phone only if you switch on cloud sync.

Kosht works without an account, and your records stay on the phone. An account is for one thing: seeing the same figures on your other phone.
At first launch you can create one, sign in, or carry on without it. Signing up asks for your email, sends a six-digit code to it, and then lets you pick a password. Forgot it later? The same code arrives by email and you set a new one.
After that everything happens by itself: records, categories, accounts, debts, goals, challenges and awards appear on your other phone as soon as you sign in there. No connection is needed to keep working — whatever you add offline goes up the moment the internet is back. Deleting something deletes it everywhere, so nothing you removed comes back.
Settings → Account shows the address, when it last synced, a button to sync right now, a switch for doing it automatically, and Sign out — which leaves every record on the phone. Receipt photos are never uploaded.
Your settings travel too: currency, theme, the interface and notification switches, the daily budget, the report you built, your name and nickname. A second phone ends up looking and behaving like the first. The interface language stays with the device, on purpose.
Receipt photos are the exception, and they are off by default — the policy says the images stay on the phone, and they do until you say otherwise. Switch on "Sync receipt photos" in the Account block and they are uploaded to a private folder only your account can read, and downloaded onto your other device. That switch is a consent of its own and is recorded as one; switching it off deletes the uploaded copies and leaves the originals here.
The sync icon sits in the row with your address: it starts a sync and turns into a spinner while one is running. Tap the row itself for the full address, the exact time of the last sync and whether automatic sync is on.

The big card shows your total balance (all income minus all expenses) with this month\'s income and expenses below it. If your currency is not BYN, the ≈ line shows the equivalent at the live rate. In the top row: the 🔥 chip is your under-budget streak, the trophy opens Achievements, the avatar is your profile. "Recent" lists the latest records — tap one to edit, "All" jumps to History. The big + button adds a transaction.

Switch Expense/Income at the top. For a new record the calculator opens by itself in a bottom sheet; type the sum (comma adds cents) and hit Apply — tap the amount any time to open it again. Pick a category in the carousel — the "New" circle creates your own with a name, icon and color. The date chip opens a calendar (defaults to today). Write an optional note. In the bottom row the scanner icon reads a receipt photo and the photo icon attaches one from camera or gallery; tap the thumbnail to view or remove it. Save finishes. When editing an existing record a trash icon appears in the top bar.

In the editor tap the scanner icon (bottom row, next to the photo icon), then shoot the receipt or pick it from the gallery.
If the receipt has a QR code, Kosht reads the shop\'s electronic receipt through it — the figures come out exact, and even a slip with nothing but a QR on it works. That receipt is saved, and the receipt icon in the editor opens it again later, with or without a connection. A code that turns out to be a loyalty card or an advert is skipped.
With no QR the photo itself is read, right on the phone. Either way a dialog shows what was found: correct the amount or the shop if needed, the date fills itself in. Apply puts everything into the form, and you can still change any of it afterwards.
The shop goes into the note. A familiar chain is recognised by name; an unfamiliar one is read off the way the slip is printed — the largest type at the top, a trade name in quotes, a legal form, the line beside the tax number. Addresses, cashiers, document headers, card details and scanning noise are thrown out, and if no line looks like a name the note is simply left empty rather than filled with something off the receipt.

Arrows switch months. The search field filters by note and custom category names. Chips: All / Expense / Income, "Category" opens a category picker (tap ✕ on the chip to clear), "Period" opens a calendar where you select a single day or a range — the period replaces month navigation until you clear it with ✕. Records are grouped by day with a net total per day. Swipe a row left to delete — an Undo snackbar appears. Tap a row to edit it.
Swiping a row deletes it and offers it back: "Transaction deleted — Undo" appears along the bottom, always above the add button, and the same offer follows a delete from the editor. The receipt photo is only thrown away once that offer has passed, so undoing really does put everything back.

Three views via the round buttons: 1) Charts — a donut of categories with the total in the middle and daily bars below; 2) Calendar — a heatmap where a darker day means more spent; tap a day to see its records; 3) Report — the verdict for a whole period, with arrows walking back through past ones. It shows spending vs the previous period of the same length, income, result, daily average, no-spend days, top category and personalized tips. Which period it covers (week, month, quarter, year) and which rows are shown are set in Settings → Report. The Expense/Income toggle applies to charts and calendar, arrows switch months.

The NBRB rates card shows official rates with the update time — the arrow button refreshes them manually; without a connection the rates from the last successful check stay on screen and a toast explains why nothing changed. Any amount in a foreign currency shows its ≈ BYN equivalent. Changing the app currency in Settings converts all stored amounts at the current rate; each expense also freezes its BYN value at payment time, so history never drifts. Recurring payments: + adds one — title, amount, currency, the charge date picked in a calendar and a frequency (weekly / monthly / every 3 months / yearly). Nothing is charged silently: due payments appear in "Awaiting confirmation", and Confirm records the expense (for a foreign currency you can adjust the rate; with several accounts you also pick which one the payment is deducted from). The switch pauses a payment, the trash deletes it.

Debts: + adds one — who, direction (I owe / owed to me), amount in any currency, note. The two tiles total both directions in BYN. Tap a debt to repay a part, close it or delete it. Goals: + creates a goal with a target amount; deposits linked to the goal fill its progress bar, and reaching the target celebrates 🎉. Savings: "Set aside" and "Withdraw" record movements (optionally toward a goal), the journal below lists them with BYN equivalents; the trash removes an entry.

Open with the trophy on Home. The streak card counts consecutive days you stayed within the daily budget (set it in Settings, auto = last month\'s average). Challenges: + creates one — Limit (spend under X, optionally in one category), No spend, or Save up (set aside X) — for a week, until month end or 30 days. Progress updates live; tap a challenge to edit its title, amount, category and end date, the trash removes it. Below are 30 awards, six to a page, easiest first: from the first record to a year inside the budget, a thousand records, five thousand saved, a perfect month without a single day over budget, three months in a row in the black, and twenty challenges completed. Tap any award to see how to earn it, your progress toward it (like "6 / 10"), and the date you earned it. An award unlocks the moment it is deserved, whichever screen you are on: a congratulation appears over the app and a quiet note lands in the shade — you never have to open this screen for it to count. Once earned an award stays yours forever, even if the streak resets.

By default there is a single account and the app looks perfectly simple. Add more (Settings → Accounts: name, icon, color — e.g. Cash, a second card) and Kosht lights up: the editor gets an account chip next to the date so you choose where the money comes from or goes to, confirming a recurring payment asks which account to deduct from, Home shows a balance pill per account under the main card, and Statistics gains an account filter. Tapping an account opens its card: the pencil (or a tap on the name) reveals renaming plus icon and color, the balance field sets the real amount, and the trash icon deletes it — its records move to the primary account.

The calculator lives in a full-width bottom sheet: it opens by itself for a new record and whenever you tap the amount. The right column of the keypad holds ÷ × − +. Type expressions like 12,50+3,90+8. While an operation is unfinished the big button turns into = — tap it to evaluate. Apply writes the result into the amount field and closes the sheet; Cancel or a swipe down leaves the amount untouched. Multiplication and division take precedence, as they should.

Profile — tap to set a photo from the gallery or one of the built-in avatars, press and hold the avatar to remove the photo, and set your name and nickname (used in greetings and reports). Interface toggles hide anything you do not need and control whether the calculator opens by itself when adding a record. The Report block sets the period the statistics report covers and ticks off exactly which metric rows it shows. Notifications: an evening reminder (only if nothing was logged), payments awaiting confirmation, a Monday summary, awards you earn, and — once signed in — whether Kosht may email you about new features. The Account block follows: tap the address row to see the full address, the exact time of the last sync and whether automatic sync is on; sign out asks first, and deleting the account and its data is the last row there. About holds the guide, the Terms, the Personal data policy and the full manual — each tap saves the PDF into your phone\'s Downloads and opens it, so it stays yours to read, print or forward. Tap Version to check for a newer build: Kosht either says you are up to date or downloads and installs the update right there — no browser, nothing left in Downloads, and your data stays in place. Android asks once for permission to let Kosht install its own updates. Offline it just says the check is not possible right now. Theme: system/light/dark plus Material You dynamic colors. Language: system, Russian or English. Currency — switching converts everything at the live NBRB rate: records, the daily budget, balance corrections, challenge limits, savings, goals, debts and recurring charges. Daily budget powers the streak.
